title: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance: policy insights columns withdrawn from the roadmap
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the withdrawn roadmap proposal from the documented hourly scanning counts, and its access-control path, command and licensing statements are supported. One minor correction should acknowledge that Microsoft's permissions table also grants alert access to the combined Communication Compliance role group, unlike the investigation page's narrower list.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft says a zero or low scanned-message count might mean the policy is too strict.
claims.quote: If the value in the column is 0 or a low number, it might be because the policy is too strict.

claims.claim: Microsoft's examples of overly restrictive scope include one user or a location the in-scope user does not use.
claims.quote: For example, the policy might be focused on just one user or on just one location that the in-scope user doesn't use.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[0].governs; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Communication Compliance roles and role-group permissions govern access to the solution and its Policies page.
claims.quote: To use any of the Communication Compliance-related tools in the Microsoft Purview portal, users need the appropriate permissions. The easiest way to assign roles is to add the user to the appropriate role group

claims.claim: The permissions page names Global Administrator and Compliance Administrator in Entra ID as roles making the solution available as a menu option.
claims.quote: To make Communication Compliance available as a menu option in Microsoft Purview portal ... Microsoft Entra ID Global Administrator role ... Microsoft Entra ID Compliance Administrator role

claims.claim: The permissions page also names Organization Management, Compliance Administrator, Communication Compliance and Communication Compliance Admins role groups for the menu option.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview portal Organization Management role group; Microsoft Purview portal Compliance Administrator role group; Communication Compliance role group; Communication Compliance Admins role group

claims.claim: Role-group membership is edited in Microsoft Purview portal at Settings > Roles and groups > Role groups > role group > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote: Select Settings ... select Roles and groups, then select Role groups ... Select the Communication Compliance role group, then select Edit. ... Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to the identified role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... The Member parameter specifies who you want to add to the role group.

claims.claim: Identity and Member are applicable to Security & Compliance, and Member accepts a UPN.
claims.quote: -Identity ... Applicable: ... Security & Compliance ... -Member ... Applicable: ... Security & Compliance ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: Role-group permission changes can take up to 30 minutes to apply.
claims.quote: After configuring your role groups, it might take up to 30 minutes for the role group permissions to apply to assigned users across your organization.

claims.claim: The Communication Compliance and Communication Compliance Admins role groups can configure policies and settings.
claims.quote: | Actions | Communication Compliance | Communication Compliance Admins | ... | Configure policies and settings | Yes | Yes | No | No | No |

claims.claim: The investigation page requires the Communication Compliance Analysts or Communication Compliance Investigators role group to view and act on alerts.
claims.quote: To view and act on alerts, assign users the following permissions: ... The Communication Compliance Analysts or the Communication Compliance Investigators role group
claims.fix: After the alert-access sentence, add: "The permissions page also lists the combined Communication Compliance role group as able to access and investigate alerts, although the investigation page names only Analysts and Investigators." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-permissions, whose table gives Yes for Communication Compliance under Access and investigate alerts.

claims.claim: Viewing and acting on alerts also requires reviewer assignment in the policy associated with the alert.
claims.quote: To view and act on alerts, assign users the following permissions: ... Reviewer in the policy that is associated with the alert

claims.claim: Administrative-unit scoping restricts which policies a role-group member can view and manage on the Policies page.
claims.quote: If your role group is scoped by one or more admin units, you see a message at the top of the page that you can only view and manage the policies that you're scoped for.

claims.claim: Administrators must verify that the organization has a supported subscription for Communication Compliance.
claims.quote: To access and use Communication Compliance, administrators need to verify that their organization has a supported subscription

claims.claim: Users must have the appropriate licenses assigned.
claims.quote: administrators need to verify that their organization has a supported subscription and that users have the appropriate licenses assigned.
